description:
fz2 run on a program building [1 | 2] panics: fz_list_cons_int ExpectedTag (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1874). At 62c02cb1a, `dbg([1 | 2])` also fails on interp: "backend list: cannot allocate list cons: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(1), found: ValueKind(13) }". Elixir builds the improper list and inspect renders [1 | 2]. Done when: an oracle fixture building, matching and inspecting improper lists agrees on interp, run and build, and fixture 00665 gains the improper `[1] ++ 2` case it had to leave out.

Also covered here: length/1 of an improper list in a guard. The guard census for GH #303 found it is an interpreter internal error and a JIT/AOT abort; Elixir's guard fails and the next clause is tried. Since fz-rs7.4 a failed operation in a guard leaves its clause unmatched, so once an improper list can be built the oracle fixture adds: def f(l) when length(l) > 0 applied to [1 | 2] answers the next clause on interp, run and build.

comments.text: fz-sc8.10 (49f85b767) deleted the renderer's improper-list branch because no list tail could be anything but a list. When [1 | 2] becomes a value, runtime/src/any_value.rs's Renderer must print it as Elixir's Inspect.Algebra.container_each does: the ... check comes first, then [left | right] renders both without charging the tail against limit (Elixir 1.19.4: inspect([1 | 2], limit: 1) = [1 | 2]; inspect([1, 2 | 3], limit: 1) = [1, ...]; inspect([1, 2 | 3]) = [1, 2 | 3]). Also: keyword? and List.ascii_printable? are false for an improper list.

title: An improper list [1 | 2] panics at runtime
